title: Saying goodbye — thanks, invitations, and promises to meet again
title_target: ভালো থাকবেন, আবার দেখা হবে — bha-lo thak-bèn, a-bar dè-kha hô-bé
goal: Give heartfelt thanks, accept and extend invitations, and part without saying “go” — a Bengali habit worth taking home.
bekal: thanking with more than just ধন্যবাদ
saying goodbye with আসি, ভালো থাকবেন, আল্লাহ হাফেজ

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — The morning of departure
dialogs.intro: Ani leaves this morning. The whole family stands at the door. Notice that nobody says “goodbye” — and that's on purpose.

lines.speaker: আম্মা:
lines.id: Leaving so early? Eat a little something first.
lines.literal: this — early — are-going? something — eat-then — go.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Auntie, you've treated me like your own daughter.
lines.literal: auntie, you — me-to — own-of — daughter-of — like — have-kept.

lines.speaker: আম্মা:
lines.id: You are my daughter. This house is your own home.
lines.literal: you — [emph] — my — daughter-indeed. this — house — your — own — house.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Take these. A gamcha and two books.
lines.literal: this — take. one — gamcha — and — two — books.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: You've done so much! I don't know how to thank you.
lines.literal: you-all — such — something — did! what — say — that — thanks — will-give.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Don't say thank you. You don't say thank you to your own people.
lines.literal: thanks — will-say — don't. own — people-to — thanks — say — not.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Just say you'll come again. That's enough.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I'll come again. I promise. And you must come too.
lines.literal: I — again — will-come. word — gave. and — you-all-too — will-come.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: To Indonesia? Inshallah! But keep in touch.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Of course. Well then … I'll be going.

lines.speaker: আম্মা:
lines.id: Travel safely, dear. Take care. Allah hafez.
lines.literal: care-with — go, daughter. well — stay. Allah — protector.

notes: ⚠️ **With people who already count as family, ধন্যবাদ actually feels cold.** It's a real culture shock: thanking your host, close friends, or family too much creates distance, as if you were treating them as outsiders. You really will hear **আপন মানুষকে ধন্যবাদ বলে না** — “you don't say thank you to your own people”. ⚠️ With vendors, drivers, and strangers, ধন্যবাদ is still normal and polite.

**The thanks people value more is naming what they did, or promising to return.** আপনারা অনেক করলেন (you've done so much), আমি আবার আসব (I'll come again), আপনাদের কথা মনে থাকবে (I'll remember you). ⚠️ These three sentences mean far more than saying ধন্যবাদ five times.

**নিজের means “one's own” and works for any owner.** নিজের বাড়ি (one's own home), নিজের মেয়ে (one's own daughter), নিজের কাজ (one's own business). ⚠️ It replaces আমার · তোমার · তার when the owner is the subject of the sentence: সে নিজের ঘরে আছে (he/she is in his/her own room) differs from সে তার ঘরে আছে (he/she is in that other person's room).

**Saying goodbye doesn't use the word “go”.** You say **আসি** (“I'm coming”) — explained in Unit 8 — or **আসছি** (“I'm on my way”). ⚠️ The warmest and safest farewell for anyone is still **ভালো থাকবেন** (stay well). To someone younger or close, it's **ভালো থেকো**.

**Farewells differ by religion, but all are well received.** **আল্লাহ হাফেজ** *allah haphéj* among Bangladeshi Muslims; **নমস্কার** or **আসি** among Hindus in West Bengal. **ইনশাআল্লাহ** is used for future plans, just as across the Muslim world.

**যোগাযোগ রাখবেন** *jogajog rakh-bèn* — “keep in touch” — is a sincere closing line, not small talk. ⚠️ In Bengal a relationship once formed isn't considered over just because someone leaves; don't be surprised to be asked how you are years later.

**সাবধানে যেয়ো — “travel safely”.** It's said to anyone leaving the house, even just for the market. Together with **ভালো থেকো** and **পৌঁছে ফোন কোরো** (call when you get there), the three make up a little package of care.

grammars.title: Thanking, saying goodbye, promising
after: ⚠️ **আবার আসবেন — “do come again” — is a sincere invitation**, and it deserves more than a smile. Answer with **অবশ্যই আসব** (I'll certainly come) or **ইনশাআল্লাহ**.

grammars.title: নিজের and inviting
after: **দাওয়াত রইল** *daoat rôilô* — literally “the invitation remains” — is the Bengali way of saying the door is always open, without setting a date. It's warm and pressure-free, and you can use it back.

blocks.text: If you've reached this page by really doing the exercises, you can now do all this in Bengali: introduce yourself, ask the way, bargain at the market, order food, explain that you're ill, make appointments, talk about yesterday, plan tomorrow, compare two things, and say goodbye politely. That's a full A1, and it's no small thing.
Four of the most useful things to do next

items: **Listen without forcing yourself to understand.** Find a Bengali news channel or podcast and let it run in the background while you do other things. Ears learn from a flood of sound, not from tidy drills.
**Watch a Satyajit Ray film with English subtitles.** The stories are slow, the dialog clear, and you'll catch far more words than you expect.

**Find one person to talk to every week.** There are Bengali communities in London, New York, Toronto, and Singapore, and almost everyone will be thrilled to hear a foreigner speak their language. Start with **আমি একটু একটু বাংলা বলি**.
**Write three sentences a day.** About anything — the weather, lunch, what you saw on the street. Three sentences a day for a month is ninety sentences, more than all the dialogs in this module.

blocks.title: The next level: what awaits at A2
items: **Compound verbs** — যেতে থাকা (keep going), করে ফেলা (get it done), বলে দেওয়া (tell, let someone know). Bengali builds subtle meanings by attaching verbs to verbs, and this is what makes speakers sound native.
**High-polite forms and the written language (সাধু ভাষা)** — the language of old newspapers, poetry, and Rabindranath's songs uses forms different from speech.
**Complex sentences with যে** — আমি জানি যে সে আসবে (I know that he/she will come). One small word that opens long sentences.
**Reading the script without the pronunciation guide.** This matters most. Start with shop signs and headlines; both are short, repetitive, and everywhere.

blocks.text: One last thing. Bengali is a language people once died to defend, and they know very well how rarely foreigners choose to learn it. Your first sentence — even if it's wrong, even if you stumble — will be met with a warmth that may make you blush. Just accept it. It isn't praise for your skill; it's thanks for taking the trouble. **শুভকামনা** *shubhôkamôna* — good luck, and **আবার দেখা হবে**.

answers: আসি। — ধন্যবাদ। — সাবধানে যাবেন। — আমাদের বাড়িতে আসবেন।
আমি আবার আসব। — যোগাযোগ রাখবেন। — ভালো থাকবেন আর সাবধানে যাবেন। — আপনাদের কথা মনে থাকবে। — আবার দেখা হবে।
আমি আবার আসব, কথা দিলাম। — ভালো থাকবেন। — সাবধানে যাবেন। — যোগাযোগ রাখবেন। — আপনারা অনেক করলেন। — আবার দেখা হবে।
